# VibeMaster > **Read this in other languages: [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)** **A local AI butler for your Mac.** VibeMaster wraps [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) (and other agent runtimes) with the things a single chat session can't give you: long-term memory, multi-agent observability, scheduling & approvals, a local skill library, and a [Feishu / Lark](https://www.feishu.cn/) bridge so you can command and approve your agents from your phone while you're away from the keyboard. The in-product assistant persona is called **Jarvis**. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) ![Platform: macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%20arm64-black) ![Built with Electron](https://img.shields.io/badge/Electron-React-47848F)

--- ## Why VibeMaster? Claude Code is a brilliant assistant with an enormous short-term memory — but it's only smart inside the one session you're talking to. VibeMaster gives it a **body** that persists across sessions and restarts: - **It remembers you** across sessions (replay + activity aggregation + plain-`.md` memory files). - **It watches every agent** running on your machine (Claude Code, Cursor, …) so you can see what each worker is doing right now. - **It acts for you** — injects keystrokes into the right terminal to Allow/Deny permission prompts, exposes a set of MCP tools, and guards against dangerous actions with a three-tier "red zone". - **It reaches you anywhere** — a Feishu/Lark long-connection bridge turns approvals and chat into interactive cards on your phone. > Claude Code is the *brain* (pluggable — swap it later). The *body* — memory, observability, control, bridge, skills — is what VibeMaster owns and what makes the brain feel like it actually knows you. ## Features | Capability | What it does | |---|---| | 🧠 **Memory** | Conversation replay, activity aggregation, and `.md` memory files that workers inherit across sessions. | | 👁️ **Watch** | Observe multiple agents (Claude Code / Cursor / …) and their live state in one dashboard. | | 🛠️ **Skills** | A local skill repository with lightweight (no-LLM) semantic matching. | | 👥 **Squads** | Reusable agent + skill + host presets you can dispatch as a unit. | | 🎛️ **Control** | TTY keystroke injection for Allow/Deny, an MCP tool server, and a three-tier red-zone safety net. | | 🔗 **Bridge** | Feishu/Lark long-connection with interactive approval cards + an in-app chat box. | | 💾 **State** | Everything local: SQLite + `~/.vibemaster/`. No cloud account, no telemetry. |


Approve or deny a permission prompt from a floating card — no need to switch back to the terminal.


An ambient pill shows what your agents are doing while you keep working.

## Architecture ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ VibeMaster (local AI butler) │ │ │ │ BODY (always on — owned by VibeMaster) │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Memory replay + activity aggregation + .md files │ │ │ │ Watch multi-agent observability (claude / cursor / …) │ │ │ │ Skills local skill repo + semantic match (no LLM call) │ │ │ │ Squads agent + skill + host presets │ │ │ │ Control TTY inject + MCP tools + 3-tier red zone │ │ │ │ Bridge Feishu/Lark long-connection + interactive cards │ │ │ │ State SQLite + ~/.vibemaster/ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ ↓ gives the brain memory / tools │ │ BRAIN (pluggable — today: Claude Code) │ │ ↓ dispatches work to │ │ WORKERS (pluggable — Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / Cursor …) │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` VibeMaster is an **Electron** app: - **`backend/`** — the Electron main process (TypeScript, `better-sqlite3` + Drizzle, the MCP server, the Feishu SDK bridge, agent watchers & control). - **`frontend/`** — the renderer UI (React + Vite + Tailwind + Radix + Zustand). - **`jetbrains-plugin/`** — a Kotlin plugin that lets VibeMaster type Allow/Deny into a JetBrains IDE terminal. - **`vscode-plugin/`** — the same bridge for VS Code / Cursor and forks. - **`scripts/`** — macOS build & install helpers. ## Requirements - **macOS on Apple Silicon (arm64).** Intel macOS / Linux / Windows are not supported yet — contributions welcome (see [Roadmap](#roadmap)). - **Node.js 18+**. - **Xcode Command Line Tools** (`xcode-select --install`) — needed to build the native `better-sqlite3` module. - **[Claude Code CLI](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code)** installed and working. - *(Optional)* A Feishu/Lark account + a self-built app, for the remote bridge. ## Quick start ### Run from source (development) ```bash # 1. Install dependencies for both workspaces cd frontend && npm install cd ../backend && npm install # 2. Terminal A — frontend dev server (Vite) cd frontend && npm run dev # 3. Terminal B — backend (tsup --watch) + Electron cd backend && npm run dev ``` ### Build a macOS app ```bash ./scripts/build-mac.sh --install # build + copy to /Applications open /Applications/VibeMaster.app ``` `build-mac.sh` builds the frontend (Vite) and backend (tsup), packages with electron-builder (arm64, ad-hoc signed), and strips the quarantine attribute so the app runs locally. Run `./scripts/build-mac.sh` for a plain build or `--open` to reveal it in Finder. > The app is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. If macOS Gatekeeper blocks it, run: > `xattr -cr /Applications/VibeMaster.app` ## Configuration (Feishu / Lark bridge) The remote bridge is optional — VibeMaster runs fully locally without it. To enable it: 1. Create a self-built app at and note its **App ID** and **App Secret**. 2. Copy the template and fill in your values: ```bash cp backend/.env.example ~/.vibemaster/.env # then edit ~/.vibemaster/.env ``` 3. The only three fields you need are your Feishu **App ID**, **App Secret**, and your own **open_id** (the single authorized user). The template explains how to find each. VibeMaster uses Feishu's **long-connection** mode, so there's no public domain, ngrok, or webhook to set up — events arrive over an outbound TLS tunnel from your machine. ## IDE bridge plugins To click **Allow / Deny** from VibeMaster when Claude Code runs inside an IDE terminal, install the matching bridge plugin: - **JetBrains** (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, GoLand, …): ```bash cd jetbrains-plugin && ./gradlew buildPlugin # install build/distributions/*.zip via Settings → Plugins → Install Plugin from Disk ``` - **VS Code / Cursor**: ```bash cd vscode-plugin && npm install && npm run package # produces a .vsix to install ``` ## Roadmap VibeMaster is **macOS / single-user** focused today. Help wanted on: - macOS x64 (Intel) support - Linux support (replacements for AppleScript / macOS permissions / Keychain) - Windows support - Tests (the project currently has none — PRs very welcome) ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. This is a young project — expect rough edges. Please: - Keep PRs focused and describe how you tested them. - Be aware this app handles Feishu tokens, local Claude Code processes, and TTY injection — be thoughtful about security-sensitive changes. ## Privacy All data stays on your machine: SQLite + `~/.vibemaster/`. Feishu tokens are only sent to Feishu's official endpoints; Claude Code conversations go through Anthropic's official API. VibeMaster itself collects **no telemetry**. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © White
